ops.title: Codex 0.155.1 native plugin paths and zero-turn resume semantics
ops.body:
# Codex CLI 0.155.1 plugin and zero-turn runtime follow-up

Date: 2026-09-22  
Scope: isolated, read-only diagnosis; no repository or user configuration changes; no model turns.

## Executive verdict

Codex CLI 0.155.1 accepts the consumers' compatibility-manifest component paths at runtime. In an isolated marketplace and `CODEX_HOME`, `skills/list` loaded all six skills from the two non-default `./codex-skills/` directories, `hooks/list` loaded the four cc-review hooks from `./codex-hooks/hooks.json`, and `mcpServerStatus/list` attributed the cc-review server declared through `./.codex-mcp.json` to the installed plugin. This is runtime load evidence, not only install/cache evidence.

The cc-present inline `"hooks":{"hooks":{}}` also behaves as intended: it replaces default `hooks/hooks.json` discovery and loads zero cc-present hooks. The official packaging documentation says an explicit hooks value replaces default-file discovery, and the runtime result agrees.

One cc-review MCP defect remains: its source declaration uses `"command":"${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/codex.sh"`. The actual declaration registered the server but failed startup with `No such file or directory`; Codex did not expand that token for the MCP executable and did not inject `PLUGIN_ROOT` into the MCP child. Replacing only the disposable MCP command with `/usr/bin/python3` plus an absolute probe-script argument made the same custom component path connect and answer a direct tool call. `PLUGIN_ROOT` expansion/injection is documented for plugin hooks, not for MCP processes.

The launcher's empty-thread handoff assumption is false on 0.155.1. `thread/start` with `ephemeral:false` creates a loaded in-memory thread and returns a rollout path, but no rollout file is written before the first turn. `thread/resume` fails with `-32600 no rollout found` even on the same initialized connection while `thread/loaded/list` still contains the ID and `thread/read` succeeds. After app-server closure, the in-memory thread disappears as well. There is no supported attach, subscribe, persist, or flush RPC for this state.

## Probe boundary

- Installed runtime: `codex-cli 0.155.1` from `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/codex/0.155.1/bin/codex`.
- Isolated root: `/tmp/codex-port-runtime-followup.8OgXha`.
- Isolated home: `/tmp/codex-port-runtime-followup.8OgXha/home`.
- Isolated `CODEX_HOME`: `/tmp/codex-port-runtime-followup.8OgXha/home/.codex`.
- Marketplace copies came from:
  - `/Users/yasyf/.orca/workspaces/cc-present/codex-present/plugin`
  - `/Users/yasyf/.orca/workspaces/cc-review/codex-consumers/plugin`
- No source plugin, repository file, user config, user auth, or existing app-server session was modified.
- The only MCP tool call targeted a disposable local read-only probe; no model request or model turn was created.

## Native plugin load evidence

### Installation

`codex plugin marketplace add` discovered both plugins, and `codex plugin add` installed enabled cache copies:

- `cc-present@runtime-probe`, version `0.33.7`
- `cc-review@runtime-probe`, version `0.36.1`

This only established the input to the load probe. The following app-server responses established actual consumption of the declared resources.

### Skills

`skills/list` with `forceReload:true` returned these plugin-owned entries, all `enabled:true`, `scope:"user"`, with paths inside the installed cache:

- `cc-present:author-pack`
- `cc-present:present`
- `cc-present:present-triage`
- `cc-review:classify-batch`
- `cc-review:organize`
- `cc-review:start`

Each entry carried its matching `pluginId`; the response reported no skill errors. The observed provenance shape was:

```text
name, path, scope, enabled, pluginId
```

### Hooks

`hooks/list` returned four cc-review hooks from the installed `codex-hooks/hooks.json` cache path:

- `sessionStart` -> `session-record`
- `preToolUse` with matcher `apply_patch|Edit|Write|NotebookEdit` -> `guard-edit`
- `userPromptSubmit` -> `turn-start`
- `stop` -> `turn-end`

Every entry had `source:"plugin"`, `pluginId:"cc-review@runtime-probe"`, `enabled:true`, and `trustStatus:"untrusted"`. `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` in each hook command was expanded to the installed plugin cache path. No cc-present hook appeared, and the response contained no errors or warnings, confirming its inline empty hook override suppressed default discovery.

The observed hook provenance shape was:

```text
eventName, handlerType, command, matcher, source, sourcePath,
pluginId, enabled, trustStatus
```

### MCP component path and launcher

With cc-review's actual `./.codex-mcp.json`, `mcpServerStatus/list` returned a server named `cc-review` with `pluginId:"cc-review@runtime-probe"`. That proves the custom manifest path was parsed and the server declaration was attached to the plugin. Startup then failed:

```text
runtimeStatus: failed
toolsError: MCP startup failed: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

The failing source declaration was:

```json
{
  "command": "${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/codex.sh",
  "args": ["mcp-channel"]
}
```

For the second run, only the disposable copy of `.codex-mcp.json` was changed to an absolute executable and probe argument. The server became `runtimeStatus:"connected"`; status exposed `serverInfo` and the `manifest_probe` tool, and `mcpServer/tool/call` returned `isError:false`. The child observed its thread cwd, `_meta` keys `progressToken` and `threadId`, and `PLUGIN_ROOT:null`.

The observed status provenance shape was:

```text
name, pluginId, runtimeStatus, authStatus, serverInfo,
tools, toolsError, resources, resourceTemplates
```

Conclusion: custom `mcpServers` path loading works; the source launch command does not. Hook-specific `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` behavior must not be assumed for MCP.

## Zero-turn lifecycle evidence

One representative generated thread ID was `01a0c78f-8098-7032-8bd8-c5d939078a14`.

Immediately after `thread/start` with `ephemeral:false`:

- the response reported `status.type:"idle"`, `turns:[]`, and an absolute rollout path;
- `thread/loaded/list` contained the ID;
- `thread/read` on the same app-server returned the in-memory thread;
- `thread/list` returned no stored threads;
- the advertised rollout path did not exist;
- the isolated state database had no thread row.

Calling `thread/resume` on that same connection returned:

```json
{
  "code": -32600,
  "message": "no rollout found for thread id 01a0c78f-8098-7032-8bd8-c5d939078a14"
}
```

The failed resume did not unload the thread: `thread/loaded/list` still contained it. After closing the app-server and starting a fresh one with the same isolated `CODEX_HOME`:

- `thread/loaded/list` was empty;
- `thread/read` returned `thread not loaded`;
- `thread/list` was empty;
- `thread/resume` returned the same `no rollout found` error.

The generated 0.155.1 schema exposes `thread/start`, `thread/resume`, `thread/unsubscribe`, and `thread/loaded/list`, but no thread attach/subscribe/persist/flush request. `ThreadStartParams.ephemeral` distinguishes in-memory-only intent from durable intent; `false` does not force a zero-turn rollout write. `ThreadResumeParams.path` and `history` are explicitly unstable, and `history` is marked for Codex Cloud only; neither is a supported persistence operation.

`codex --remote ADDR resume ID` therefore cannot attach to this zero-turn thread: the TUI bootstrap must call the same failing `thread/resume`. Closing or retaining the originating client connection does not change that result.

## Attachment and terminal ownership

The public protocol has no observable per-thread subscriber, current-client, or terminal-owner field in 0.155.1:

- `initialize.clientInfo` identifies one transport connection to the server, not a thread attachment visible to other clients.
- `Thread.originator` is documented as creation-time provenance independent of the current client or executor.
- `Thread.canAcceptDirectInput` says whether the loaded runtime accepts direct turns; it does not identify who is attached.
- `thread/loaded/list` and runtime `status` do not expose subscriber presence.

Consequently, desktop-versus-CLI terminal ownership cannot be fenced from native thread metadata. A launcher must retain its own connection/terminal lifecycle state or add an application-level lease.

## Supported launcher choices

1. Preferred for current 0.155.1: start the remote TUI without `resume` (`codex --remote ADDR -C CWD`) so the TUI owns `thread/start`, then discover/bind the resulting ID after startup. This reverses the planned ordering but does not require a synthetic turn.
2. If the launcher must create the thread first, keep control through the app-server protocol and submit the user's real first turn on that loaded thread. Only hand it to `resume` after that real turn has caused a durable rollout to exist. This is not an empty-thread handoff and must account for turn/approval ownership.
3. If create-ID-then-empty-TUI-resume is a hard requirement, pin 0.150.1, where the upstream reproducer reports zero-turn rollout persistence still worked, and track the open regression before upgrading.

Do not use a dummy/model turn only to materialize storage. Do not treat `thread/read`, `loaded/list`, `ephemeral:false`, the advertised path, or unstable `history`/`path` resume inputs as a durability acknowledgment.

## Recommendations for the consumer plugins

- Keep the cc-present manifest shape: its custom skill path loads correctly and the inline empty hooks object successfully suppresses the inherited default hook file.
- Keep cc-review's `skills` and `hooks` path declarations; both load correctly in 0.155.1.
- Change cc-review's MCP deployment assumption. A local MCP command must be resolvable without hook-only `PLUGIN_ROOT` expansion/injection, or the MCP should use a supported remote streamable-HTTP endpoint. The disposable absolute-command proof is diagnostic, not a portable package prescription.
- Add a runtime smoke test that asserts plugin IDs on `skills/list`, `hooks/list`, and `mcpServerStatus/list`, then directly calls one MCP tool. Manifest validation or successful plugin installation is insufficient.
- Treat plugin hooks as installed but untrusted until the user reviews them; the probe deliberately did not bypass hook trust or execute hook bodies.

## Evidence files

- Actual consumer declarations: `/tmp/codex-port-runtime-followup.8OgXha/observations-actual-consumer.json`
- Disposable absolute-command MCP proof: `/tmp/codex-port-runtime-followup.8OgXha/observations-disposable-mcp.json`
- App-server wire transcript for actual declarations: `/tmp/codex-port-runtime-followup.8OgXha/app-server-actual-consumer.jsonl`
- App-server wire transcript for disposable MCP proof: `/tmp/codex-port-runtime-followup.8OgXha/app-server-disposable-mcp.jsonl`
- Generated protocol schema: `/tmp/codex-port-runtime-followup.8OgXha/schema/`
- Probe harness and marketplace copies: `/tmp/codex-port-runtime-followup.8OgXha/`

## Primary documentation and corroboration

- OpenAI plugin packaging and path rules: https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins
- OpenAI Codex App Server protocol and lifecycle: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server
- Open upstream zero-turn regression with the same minimal sequence: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/42099
- Open upstream request for subscriber presence, confirming the current protocol gap: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35676
